utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is case number IT-98-32/1-PT, The Prosecutor versus Milan Lukic and Sredoje Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar, for that pro-activity while I'm trying to adjust my chair. Good afternoon to everyone. Before I proceed, I would like to see whether the interpretation is functioning as it should. So I ask first, Mr. Milan Lukic whether you can hear what I'm saying. THE ACCUSED MILAN LUKIC: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Sredoje Lukic, you're nodding in the affirmative. Thank you. With that we could move to the representation. Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Good afternoon, counsel. My name is Mark Harmon, appearing with me, Mr. Frederic Ossogo and our case manager Verica Balikic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Before we see where we are on the accused side. Let me first assure you, Mr. Milan Lukic, that your submissions in relation to you're assigned counsel has been received. I believe that you are engaged in a discussion with the registry where the matter now rests in resolving this. For the purposes of this Status Conference, you are represented by Mr. Yatvin, I believe, and I believe also that he is present in the courtroom. I see and recognise him. And as far as the accused Sredoje Lukic is concerned, the representation is?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. I'm Djuro Cepic Defence counsel for Mr. Sredoje Lukic. On my left-hand side is Mr. Jens Dieckmann as a co-counsel. In our Defence team on my right-hand side is our assistant Madam Christina Kerll. And just if you allow me to say, I'm very grateful and -- because you granted this postponement of this Status Conference. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Cepic. And it was no interference with my other duties to postpone it and I hope everybody else was comfortable with kicking back the time by 45 minutes. Thank you. Well, the purpose of this Status Conference is slightly different than when we last met on the 11th of June. Now the smoke has cleared, as it were, in the meaning that the uncertainty as to whether this case for both of the accused was to be referred has now been finally resolved and the case rests firmly with this Tribunal. So the purpose of this Status Conference is now to take stock on where we are on outstanding motions and also adopt a Work Plan in order to see to it that all pre-trial matters are dealt with swiftly and that we can get this case to a trial. So let me first start then with pending motions. Have I three noted on my list, and I know that hopefully this squares with the understanding of the parties, given the 65 ter Conference that you had yesterday. The first motion is a motion for disclosure which, in the wake of the final decision by the Referral Bench has been remitted to this case and that is an a motion by Mr. Cepic, and as I said it deals with disclosure. In anticipation that the matter of disclosure will finally, I hope, be dealt with when we come to the part of the Work Plan, it would I think from a tidying point of view, Mr. Cepic, if you were minded to withdraw that motion. The option is that we could find it answered by the Work Plan but I think it is simpler if you considered it to be what I think is the prudent step to withdraw the motion. I would like to hear your comment on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Absolutely, Your Honour. We with withdraw that motion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you. We note that this matter is dealt with by the withdrawal of that motion. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: The second motion is a motion filed by the Prosecution on the 3rd of April, 2007, and it deals with protective measures and has a -- is a confidential motion that has an ex parte annex to it. It seems that that is understandable, given the circumstances with the discussions with the Referral Bench involved, that there has not been a reply to this motion yet. I wonder whether the parties could confirm the accused counsel whether there is a rely to this motion from the Prosecution on protective measures.

utterances.speaker: MR. YATVIN
utterances.text: Your Honour, there is not a reply in light of the procedural posture that we were in at the time, there was not really an appropriate time to reply.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Yatvin. Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: At this moment, I can say there is no need for reply. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: That was even more clarifying. Thank you very much. I think then for the sake of, again, orderliness, if could I ask the Prosecution to take the trouble of refiling this motion, which would mean that a new time for reply would then start. That would give you, Mr. Yatvin, a chance, if you're minded to reply to do so. And also you, Mr. Cepic, to -- if you want to confirm your position, you have today to do that. So that motion is -- I can see by the nod by Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, we will refile the motion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much for that. The third pending motion that I have noted is a motion by Mr. Cepic for Sredoje Lukic. And it deals with a matter in relation to the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina seeking an order for evidence to be produced by that state. And that motion will be dealt with in due course. So those are the three motions that I have detected. Would the counsel for both sides be of the understanding that this is all?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Yatvin.

utterances.speaker: MR. YATVIN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. That clears the table, as it were. And we could then move to the prospect of adopting a Work Plan. I know that some date have been discussed yesterday and I just want to primarily see whether those dates reported to me still are valid. We first have the matter of the disclosure under Rule 66(A)(i) and that is the supporting material to the indictment. It seems that that was filed on the 18th of January, 2006. And if that is so, we don't need to spend more time on that. It seems by nods all around that that is a common understanding. The second is for disclosure then yet to be had under Rule 66(A)(ii), witness statements; we have Rule 68, exculpatory information to be disclosed which is always an ongoing obligation; and finally, we have the question of Rule 66(B) material, which is the right for the counsel for accused to inspect whatever material in shape and form of books and documents, et cetera, which the Prosecution may possess. It has indicated -- indicated to me that the parties would be comfortable with the six-week time-limit for all these three, meaning that the 15th of October would be the date where the Prosecution should at the latest time fulfil obligations under 66(A)(ii), 68 and for Rule 66(B) to apply. Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: That is quite satisfactory, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: And that meets with the minds of the accused as well?

utterances.speaker: MR. YATVIN
utterances.text: Your Honour, it does with the one caveat which the Court already raised, the elephant in the room, of course, is the status of counsel for Mr. Lukic. Mr. Lukic has raised the matter with the registry and I have supported his application but, obviously, a decision has to be made at the registry, at least initially. If there is a change in counsel and depending on when that happens if it is later rather than sooner if it happens at all, it may result in the dates that you're about to go through here today. They're an application for some alteration of those dates on the part of Mr. Lukic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Yatvin. It goes without saying that a Work Plan, even if the intention only to be firm as to dates, is always subject to modifications as the case may occur. And as you rightly point out, Mr. Yatvin, we have the uncertainty, if you will, of the representation for Mr. Lukic. I saw you, Mr. Lukic, Mr. Milan Lukic, you raised your hand. You want to add something to this? Please go ahead. THE ACCUSED MILAN LUKIC: [Interpretation] Yes, by your leave, I have something to say. Since the registry refused to appoint counsel of my choice, even though that counsel fulfils all requirements of The Hague Tribunal and has in the past defended accused before this Tribunal, I have no other choice but to defend myself. I have no other option open to me. You know that for quite some time I have had no contact with my current counsel, and this is what I have decided. I believe that I'm denied -- that if I'm denied counsel of my choice, that my fundamental human rights are violated. That's all I have to say. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lukic. Well, we understand this is what you have also put in your submissions to the Chamber and as I indicated initially, the way the rules are designed it is not primary for the Chamber at this moment to address the matter of your representation. It rests, as you are well aware, with the registry. And at one point, the registry will then make a decision and that decision has not yet been made. And once that decision is made other rules come into play and eventually, it may or it may not reach the Chamber. So as for now, as I said, your representation under the rules of the Tribunal, even if you may not like it, it is the fact that Mr. Yatvin is your legally assigned counsel. But as Mr. Yatvin pointed out should changes happen here, we also obviously need to take that into account when we deal with times for various things to happen under the yet to be adopted Work Plan. But Mr. Lukic your concern has now, again, for the record been noted. Thank you very much. Mr. Yatvin.

utterances.speaker: MR. YATVIN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't want to beat this death. I just do want to point out that my silence in the face of certain allegations regarding my representation should not be read as an agreement or acquiescence; I'm addressing it in the appropriate form with the registry and I, as I said, have supported Mr. Lukic's request without agreeing that all of the allegations are accurate or that any of them are accurate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Yatvin. As you can understand from point of view, I did not have any intention to go into a matter which is dealt with at the moment with the registry. So in no way did I interpret your silence to be an acquiescence of whatever Mr. Lukic put to us. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. YATVIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Now with this, I think we could move to other matters which need to be part of the Work Plan, and it is then the obligation for the counsel or for the accused to notify the Prosecution of any alibi or special Defence that it wants to put. And the time I had in mind, which was discussed yesterday with the 65 ter Conference, is the 15th of November for that. That is a month after the full disclosure has happened. The time then for -- filing of 94 bis expert reports and also motions from the Prosecution under Rule 92 bis ter and quater, i.e. written witness submissions, the mind -- the time that has been offered and discussed is the 15th of February, 2008. We then have questions of adjudicated facts, agreed facts and stipulations on the indictment and motions pertaining to that matter should be filed not later than the 29th of February, 2008. It seems that next year is a leap year. We then come to times for pre-trial briefs and the Prosecution pre-trial brief should be filed not later than 14th of March, 2008. Pre-trial briefs for the Defence should be filed not later than the 25th of April, 2008. And if everything goes according to this Work Plan, the case would then be ready and a pre-trial conference to be determined at a later stage. When it comes to anticipation of the length of the case,, obviously the material yet to be filed is to be the determining factor here, but, I guess, that from the Prosecution's point of view it would be possible today to offer an indication as to the scope of the Prosecution's case. Obviously, this will not be held against you, Mr. Harmon, but a tentative assessment would be welcome.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. As I said yesterday at the 65 ter Conference, we believe that we could put in our case in chief in four months.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Harmon, four months. As the parties are well aware, the question of when this case then will be docketed or ready for trial is a matter which is not for this Chamber only to decide what with the indication and the timely meeting of the requirements of the Work Plan, the hope is that this case could perhaps, given other plans in other cases that also wants to compete for the infrastructure as it were, i.e. the number of judges and the number the courtrooms be ready to be docketed some time after summer or early the following year. The summer of next year, early the following year, that's the indication that we can offer. This is no news to the parties. It seems then that the times with the caveats what we have introduced are met with the parties understanding and I will now, in order to avoid further written communication on this, I will then formally as of this moment adopt the Work Plan and read it into the record so I would appreciate if the parties could take note. The first point is then disclosure under 66(A)(ii), Rule 68 and the inspection under Rule 66(B) to happen not later than 15th of October, 2007. Point number 2: Notice by Defence under Rule 67 to be filed not later than 15th of November, 2007. Point number 3: Expert reports under 94 bis and motions under 92 bis ter and quater to be filed not later than 15th of February, 2008. Point number 4: Motions in relation to adjudicated facts, agreed facts and other stipulations in relation to the indictment should be filed not later than the 29th of February, 2008. Point 5: Prosecution's pre-trial brief to be filed not later than 14th of March, 2008. Point number 6: Defence pre-trial brief to be filed not later than 25th of April, 2008. So with these six points, we have now established a Work Plan to which the parties are to be guided by. I think it is prudent also to look a bit ahead for the next Status Conference. Given the 120-day period, four-month interval that would actually mean that we could end up in the winter recess; in order to forestall that, I suggest and this I believe is also a date that was aired yesterday at the 65 ter Conference, is that we hold the next Status Conference on the 11th of December, 2007, to be preceded by 65 ter Conference on the 10th of December. Do the parties have any questions as to this Work Plan? My intention is now to move away from it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: The Prosecution has no questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Mr. Yatvin.

utterances.speaker: MR. YATVIN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't know if this is the appropriate junction or not but at the conference yesterday, I had raised the issue of possible amendments to the indictment and that I had suggested that it might be appropriate to have a deadline, obviously, without waiving the right of the Defence because they don't know what they might be to make Delic objections but it seems that if the Work Plan is to have any meaning, there needs to be some point at which we know what the charges are finally going to be, if there are going to be any changes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Sorry, so I understand, Mr. Yatvin, are you indicating that the Prosecution has indicated that they will move for amendments to the indictment?

utterances.speaker: MR. YATVIN
utterances.text: Not necessarily but the spectre has been raised and since there is the potential, it seems to me that there should be some horizon on that potential.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Yatvin. Well, Mr. Harmon, do we have any comment on this? I was unaware that this has been indicated that you were contemplating an amendment to the indictment.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have raised with counsel the possibility of an amendment. I will not be lead counsel in this case, we are restaffing this case, so other counsel will be substituting in my place. I need to consult with that other counsel once the change has been made, and one of the issues I intend to raise with new counsel is the possibility of amending this indictment to add some additional charges in respect of Milan Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Well, I think this might have been put on the table and I'm in sympathy with Mr. Yatvin indicated there should be for this a time for the Prosecution to abide by. And I suggest, Mr. Harmon, that we then add to the Work Plan that any motion for a change of the present indictment is to be filed not later than the 15th of November. That, I guess, should give you time to consult with whoever is taking over.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: That is satisfactory, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: So with the addition that we now have on the 15th of November also a time for which the Prosecution is bound to file any changes to the indictment and after that it is too late. We then move to other matters and there are very few, namely -- I am obliged, although I can see from both Mr. Milan Lukic and Mr. Sredoje Lukic that the status of your health seems to be in order, is there anything in relation to that that you wish to share with me? If need be, we can go into private session. But if you think that you don't have anything to -- to add regarding your personal situation at the detention unit, we could keep it the way it is. Mr. Milan Lukic. THE ACCUSED MILAN LUKIC: [Interpretation] Well, I have this problem with the lawyer. We cannot impose counsel on somebody in the twenty-first century and the trial is forthcoming and the trial should begin as soon as possible. That's all. My grandfather told me that in Communist times counsel were imposed on -- on the accused, by I thought that time was over. This problem needs to be resolved as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Lukic. I take it you don't have anything to add apart from your previous submissions regarding counsel and it is, Mr. Lukic, a bit premature to say whether the matter will be resolved. You may be anticipating the worst, so we will see what the registry will offer as far as a decision. Mr. Sredoje Lukic, do you have anything to comment on regarding your situation? THE ACCUSED SREDOJE LUKIC: [Interpretation] No, no. I have nothing to say. Everything is fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much for that. It is now reflected in the record. Well, this brings what I had on my agenda so before we adjourn, I would like to ask counsel whether they have any other matter which needs to be raised. Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: There's nothing on behalf the Prosecution, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Harmon. Mr. Yatvin.

utterances.speaker: MR. YATVIN
utterances.text: Nothing on behalf of Mr. Milan Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Same sentence for me, just in relation to Sredoje Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Sorry, I missed the part -- could you take that again?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour. Probably my English is not too during this day, because too many activities. I have nothing to raise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: That was a negative. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Well, that being the case, this Status Conference is now adjourned

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 4.13 p.m.
